definition: What a product is to this organisation, deciding whether it may be bought, made, used or sold. A product may be more than one kind at once.

values.name: Raw material
values.definition: An ingredient or substance that enters a formulation.

values.name: Packaging component
values.definition: A container, closure, label, case or divider.

values.name: Indirect material
values.definition: Used in production without entering the product.

values.name: Part-made good
values.definition: Made and used internally; neither bought nor sold.

values.name: Consumer unit
values.definition: The unit a consumer buys.

definition: How specific a recipe is, from the general recipe the company holds to the instructions issued for one batch, following the ISA-88 standard. Each level is written from the one above it.

values.name: General recipe
values.definition: The formulation and method, naming no factory.

values.name: Site recipe
values.definition: Adapted to the materials and constraints of one site.

values.name: Master recipe
values.definition: Bound to one work centre, with its settings.

values.name: Control recipe
values.definition: The instructions issued for one batch. This is what runs.

values.name: Site

values.name: Area

values.name: Storage zone
values.definition: A work centre for holding material.

values.name: Work unit
values.definition: One part of a work centre performing one function.

values.name: Equipment module
values.definition: One part of a unit performing one task.

definition: Why production stopped, chosen from a governed list so that stoppages can be counted and compared by reason. It does not say how long the stoppage lasted.

values.name: Cleaning

values.name: Material shortage

values.name: Quality hold

values.name: Upstream blockage

values.name: Downstream blockage

values.name: Labour unavailable
values.definition: No qualified operator available.

values.name: Utility failure

values.name: Return to supplier
